stem: A new auto-rickshaw in Dhaka, Bangladesh, is bought for 400,000 taka. Its value, in taka, \(t\) years after it is bought is modeled by \(V(t) = 400{,}000(0.85)^{t}\). According to the model, after how many whole years will the value of the auto-rickshaw first be less than half of its original value?
solution: Half of the original value is reached when \((0.85)^{t} < 0.5\).
With a calculator, \((0.85)^{4} \approx 0.522\) (more than half) and \((0.85)^{5} \approx 0.444\) (less than half).
So the value first drops below half after 5 years.

explanation.A: Incorrect. This treats the loss as \(15\%\) of the original value every year (\(4 \times 15\% = 60\%\)). The model takes \(15\%\) of the current value each year, so after 4 years about \(52\%\) remains.
explanation.B: Incorrect. \((0.85)^{3} \approx 0.614\), so after 3 years about \(61\%\) of the value remains, which is more than half.
explanation.C: Incorrect. This is roughly \(100 \div 15\), the time for the value to reach zero under a constant yearly loss. The model never reaches zero, and it passes half well before 7 years.
explanation.D: Correct. \((0.85)^{5} \approx 0.444 < 0.5\), while \((0.85)^{4} \approx 0.522\) is still above half.

verify:
t = next(n for n in range(1, 100) if Rational('0.85')**n < Rational(1, 2))
assert t == 5
assert value(choices[answer]) == 5
assert all(value(choices[k]) != 5 for k in choices if k != answer)
